chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who entrusts a drinker of wine with an amanah (trust/pledge) after knowing it in him, then there is no guarantee for him from Allah, nor is there any reward for him, nor a compensation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entrusting a known wine-drinker with a trust?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the practical implications of 'amanah' (trustworthiness) in social and financial dealings, noting that while a wine-drinker is not necessarily a disbeliever, their known vice invalidates the spiritual guarantee for the one who entrusts them. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that specific moral defects can impact the validity of trust in worldly transactions, linking the Prophet's statement to the broader concept of divine accountability for negligence in selecting trustworthy agents.
